title: The wall-exposure rule
process: which water counts against a building, and the level it is given
executor: node (CPU surface solver) and browser (GPU); raw measurements in street/raw/, scored by run.mjs
equations: water counts where it is at least 10 cm deep on an open cell within 2 m of the building and its 4-connected wet patch touches a street cell or covers at least 200 m^2
the wall level is the highest water level among the cells that count
initialConditions: not a simulation: hand-made depth grids
geometry: a 40 x 40 m lot grid at 1 m with one 8 x 8 m building and a street along the south edge; one case on the same lot at 2 m cells

lot.unit: cells, m, m, m (x0, y0, x1, y1), m

value.what: 15 cm at the wall, joined to street water
15 cm pond of 100 m^2 against the wall, not joined to the street
15 cm pond of exactly 200 m^2, not joined to the street
15 cm pond of 199 m^2, not joined to the street
9.9 cm at the wall, joined to street water
exactly 10 cm at the wall, joined to street water
15 cm joined to the street, 3 m from the wall
15 cm joined to the street, on the second cell from the wall (1-2 m)
a 100 m^2 pond that touches street water only corner to corner
two street-joined strips at different levels: the higher one
50 cm against the wall, linked to the street only by 5 cm of water
at 2 m cells: 15 cm joined to the street on the cell 2-4 m from the wall

ruleCases.unit: water boxes [x0, y0, x1, y1, depth] in m, later boxes overwrite earlier ones; hand: the answer by the rule as written

solver: src/damage.js openWater and exposure, called as app/map.js calls them (ring 2 cells, minDepth 0.10 m, the patch filter on)

reference.sources: the rule as stated in src/damage.js and in the product brief
reference.independence: written from the stated rule with union-find patches and a reach in metres; src/damage.js floods patches from a stack and steps a ring in cells

outputs: per case: whether the building is exposed, and the wall level
criteriaNotes: A decision is right or wrong; a level is exact to round-off. Predicted before running: R12 fails (src/damage.js steps two cells out whatever the cell size; the app only calls it at 1 m).
assumptions: the peak-depth grid is the input, as in the app
limitations: the rule joins patches on the peak grid: water that was never joined at one moment can count as joined
the product's own Python copy of the rule (Climate Inspection tools/gate2/wall.py) is not tested here
validRange: the rule's logic on a 1 m grid
scoring: automated: street/score.mjs builds rows with lib/score.mjs row(); one row set per executor (cpu, gpu), never merged; a case with no raw file is listed as not run and has no rows

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before any sandbox case was run
